newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Sustainability the key to EMU - Dutch central banker.
newsitem.headline: Sustainability the key to EMU - Dutch central banker.

text.p: Sustainability is the key criterion for determining which European Union (EU) members qualify for economic and monetary union (EMU), incoming Dutch central bank president Arnout Wellink said on Wednesday.

Addressing a conference, he said it was crucial that EU countries try to limit budget deficits to three percent of gross domestic product (GDP), one of the three criteria for determining EMU membership.
But he said it was silly to ask if countries with budget deficits of 2.9 percent or 3.1 percent of GDP could join a European single currency when it begins in January 1999.
"Sustainability is the relevant criterion," he told business leaders at a conference on EMU.

Wellink takes over on July 1 as president of the Dutch central bank from Wim Duisenberg, who will become the head of the European Monetary Institute, the forerunner of the first European central bank.

He said the Maastricht Treaty, which sets out the path toward EMU, even referred to a situation where a country with a budget deficit below the three percent limit may still not qualify because its budgetary position was not sustainable.
Wellink had been asked if he was afraid that the decision on who qualifies for EMU would be taken on political rather than economic grounds if France and Germany did not meet the budgetary criteria.
Earlier, he told the conference it was uncertain if next week's European summit would agree on a budget stability pact, which tries to ensure fiscal discipline among EMU participants.
